key_insight: UR-VC shows that normalized demonstration time is an imperfect proxy for task progress in robot learning, and proposes a way to automatically correct these noisy progress/value labels without manual annotation. This helps dense supervision better reflect true physical task completion, especially in contact-rich manipulation.
problem_solved: Robot learning often needs dense progress or value signals, but these are expensive to label at scale. The paper addresses the mismatch between time-derived progress labels and actual physical progress, which can mislead policy learning and task completion detection.
method: Starts from time-derived progress proxies computed from demonstration timestamps.
Learns an unsupervised correction mechanism to adjust noisy progress/value labels toward more physically meaningful targets.
Uses the corrected value signal to improve intermediate-state evaluation and downstream robot learning tasks.
impact: For practitioners, UR-VC offers a scalable way to get better dense supervision without manual labeling. This can improve training stability, progress estimation, and completion detection in robotic manipulation systems.

paper_title: UR-VC: Unsupervised Robotic Value Correction for Time-Derived Progress Proxies
paper_authors: Lirui Zhao, Modi Shi, Li Chen, Qi Liu, Ping Luo
